newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia gives Bre-X/Barrick Busang deadline.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia gives Bre-X/Barrick Busang deadline.

text.p: Indonesia's Mines and Energy Minister has set a deadline for Canadian mining firms Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp to settle with their local partners over the giant Busang gold find, ministery secretary-general Umar Said said.
He did not disclose the deadline in a conversation with reporters on Friday night.
But he earlier told Reuters the ministry had sent the letter to Bre-X and Barrick on Friday.
A ministry source close to the negotiations told Reuters on Saturday the deadline was one month from the date the letter was sent.
"They must report to the government within one month," the source, who asked not to be named, said.
In Toronto, Bre-X spokesman Steve McAnulty said the company had not yet received an official response from the Indonesian government on its joint venture proposal with Barrick.
"We have not had any official response that I know of from the government," McAnulty said.
Umar told Reuters on Friday: "We have replied to the letter from Bre-X and Barrick today. The letter says, among other things, that they must settle with their local partners soon."

He gave no further details, but the ministry source said the government "understood" an agreement between Barrick and Bre-X to divide the richest parts of the Busang gold deposit 67.5 percent for Barrick, 22.5 percent for Bre-X and 10 percent for the Indonesian government.
On Tuesday, as Barrick and Bre-X awaited a government response to their proposal, Canadian miner Placer Dome Inc made a US$5 billion merger offer to Bre-X.
Bre-X estimates the Busang find contains at least 57 million ounces of gold currently worth over $21 billion.
